missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Строй' stays in the nominative as the subject of the sentence. This is a soft masculine noun, and 'ровным' is the instrumental predicate after 'был'.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Строй' is the accusative direct object of 'построил'; as an inanimate masculine noun it matches the nominative form. 'Новый' agrees with it.
Strategic focus: Genitive after preposition. 'Строя' is the genitive after 'из' to mean out of the formation. This phrase also commonly means to break down or fall out.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'В строю' uses the special locative form 'строю' after 'в' to express standing in formation. 'Солдаты' is the nominative plural subject.
Strategic focus: Dative of direction. 'Строю' is the dative after 'к' to show movement toward the formation. 'Офицер' is the nominative subject of 'идёт'.
Strategic focus: Instrumental object. 'Строем' is the instrumental required by the verb 'гордится', which governs the instrumental. 'Этим' agrees in the masculine instrumental.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'О строе' uses the standard prepositional form 'строе' after 'о' to talk about the formation. A useful contrast with the locative 'в строю'.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Строи' is the nominative plural subject. 'Разные' agrees in the plural, and 'на площади' gives the prepositional location.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Строй' is the accusative direct object of 'проверяет'. 'Сержант' is the nominative subject, and 'внимательно' adds the manner.
Strategic focus: Nominative exclamation. 'Строй' stays in the nominative in this exclamation. 'Какой' and 'ровный' both agree in the masculine, expressing approval.
